samples.summary: MemDocStore.setBlockType still injects an empty inline into table blocks, contradicting the new "a table block's inlines is always []" invariant the YorkieDocStore change relies on
samples.evidence: The diff added `type !== 'table'` to both the CRDT and cached-model branches of `YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1494), justified by "a table node's children are its rows (`block.inlines` is always `[]`)". The sibling `DocStore` implementation was not updated: `packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:262` still runs `else if (block.inlines.length === 0) { block.inlines = [{ text: '', style: {} }] }` unconditionally, so retyping a table block through the Mem-backed editor (docs standalone harness, slides text boxes, and every `MemDocStore` test) produces a table block carrying a phantom inline while the Yorkie-backed editor produces none. Both stores are reachable behind the same `DocStore` interface (packages/docs/src/store/store.ts:110) and the same `EditorAPI.setBlockType` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3034), so the two backends now disagree on the model shape.

samples.summary: The inline-style clear path still uses the subtree-spanning `removeStyleByPath` the diff replaced everywhere else
samples.evidence: `removeNodeStyle` was introduced (yorkie-doc-store.ts:273) precisely because `removeStyleByPath(path, path+1, …)` "looks node-scoped but is not: that path range spans the node's whole subtree", and the block-type (1459), cell-style (2470) and cell-span (2520) sites were converted. `applyInlineStyle` at yorkie-doc-store.ts:1918 still calls `tree.removeStyleByPath([...blockPath, i], [...blockPath, i + 1], removeAttrs)` — the very call shape the new helper exists to avoid. It is safe today only because an inline node's children are text nodes (no element nodes to over-remove), an assumption nothing enforces; the repo's own task note records it as knowingly left behind (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:194).

samples.summary: PDF export still maps a cleared ('') color to pure black while the canvas now paints it as the theme default
samples.evidence: The diff redefines the empty-string color as *unset* on every canvas path (`resolveStoredColor` in paint-layout.ts:384/453/555 and table-renderer.ts:464/573) and as *dropped* on the DOCX/PPTX sinks. The PDF sink was routed through `toRgbHexColor` but kept its black fallback: `styleColor` (pdf-style-map.ts:151-155) returns `{0,0,0}` when the normalizer yields `undefined`, which is exactly the `''` case. Its consumers — pdf-painter.ts:389, 706 and pdf-table-painter.ts:178 — therefore export a run whose color the user explicitly cleared as black rather than the `Theme.defaultColor` ink now painted on screen (packages/docs/src/view/theme.ts:49/80, which is a palette ink and, in the dark palette, light). Same model value, two different results across the screen/PDF pair.

samples.summary: `PRST_BY_KIND` is not exhaustiveness-checked against `ShapeKind`, so a kind added later silently exports as `rect`
samples.evidence: `kindToPrst` changed from an identity mapping to `PRST_BY_KIND.get(kind) ?? 'rect'`. The `as const satisfies readonly Exclude<ShapeKind, 'freeform'>[]` annotation only proves each listed literal *is* a valid kind — it does not prove every kind is listed, so nothing (tsc included) fails when a new member is added to the `ShapeKind` union at packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:54-125. The consequence is silent: the shape exports as a rectangle instead of failing loudly. I compared the current union against the list entry-by-entry and found no omission today, so this is a forward-looking gap rather than a live regression; a `Record<Exclude<ShapeKind,'freeform'>, string>` source object (converted to a Map) would make it enforced.
searchedFor: Grep 'ShapeKind =' in packages/slides/src/model/*.ts and read element.ts:54-125
Grep 'prst|ShapeKind' in packages/slides/src/import/pptx/shape.ts (importer clamps unknown prst to 'rect')
